borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development, due to its scale, siting, and design, would appear overly dominant compared to the original dwelling, introducing a fragmented roof form and eroding the openness of a characteristic gap at a prominent corner plot. It would disrupt the surrounding pattern of development, unbalance the semi-detached pair, and detract from the distinctive ‘book-end’ typology. As such, the proposal would cause undue harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area, contrary to policies that seek to protect local character and promote good design:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2 and DMD1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)

<p>The proposed development, lacksclarity regarding its suitability for a disabled user, failing to ensure adequate wheelchair and impaired accessibility throughout the extension. Despite the presence of a ramp, the first-floor bedroom remains inaccessible, with no lift or turning circles provided, resulting in a poor-quality living environment. As such, the proposal fails to meet inclusive design standards, leading to unacceptable accommodation that is contrary to:</p><ul><li>National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)</li><li>Policies D4 and D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)</li><li>Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (February 2012)</li></ul>
description: Construction of a part two storey part single storey side and rear extension
